overall: Stabiliser (CYA) read **5** on both tests. Without stabiliser, sunlight burns off chlorine within a few hours, which likely explains free chlorine falling from **2.33** to **0.25**. Step 5 matters more than its position suggests.
pH rose from **6.9** to **8.7** in five days. Salt-chlorine pools tend to push pH up, so check pH more often than weekly for a while.

3: Acid lowers alkalinity as well as pH. Finish step 2 and retest before adding acid.

overall: Alkalinity **0** with pH **8.1** is unlikely to be real: free chlorine at **15** can throw off both tests. Retest alkalinity and pH once chlorine is back to **1–4** before adding the full **12 lb 10 oz**.

The 5-inch drain lowered calcium from **671** to **603**, about **10%**. Roughly three more 1-foot drains would be needed to get under **400**. Finish draining before steps 2–5, or the new chemicals get drained away too.

Stabiliser is still **5** after three tests. Without it, sunlight burns chlorine off fast, so chlorine at **15** may fall on its own within a day or two; worth asking the store whether waiting is an option instead of neutraliser.

1: Evaporation leaves calcium behind and topping up adds more, so only draining and refilling lowers it.
3: Turn off fountains and waterfalls for now: splashing pushes pH up.
